identity.institution: University of Oxford, Howey Research Group
identity.notes: 27 NCA/graphite 18650 cells (28 declared); Oxford path-dependent degradation in three parts; Panasonic NCR18650BD at 24 °C; CC/CC-CV cycling at C/4 or C/2; count includes 6 auxiliary half/full-cell reference files; Raj et al. Batteries & Supercaps 2020

conditions.protocol_charge_raw: CC-CV charge at C/2 to 4.2 V until C/60 (reference tests)
conditions.protocol_discharge_raw: Reference CC/CC-CV discharge at C/2 to 2.5 V; pseudo-OCV discharge at C/24; aging groups combine CC/CC-CV cycling at C/4 or C/2 with calendar storage at 90% SOC or 4.2 V

content.cycle_basis: none in the tables; each MAT-file is one test of one cell (cycling groups and EIS)
content.count_basis: 28 cells in the full study per the author documentation; no cycle total (an earlier estimate was removed).

quality.notes: Measurements are MATLAB table objects, decoded from the MCOS subsystem. Part 1 groups age from beginning of life; parts 2 and 3 continue after middle of life. Table columns TestTime and Amphr have no unit in the file. n_entities (27) is not a clean cell count: it mixes genuine numbered battery cells (20 numbered Cell IDs among Cell1..Cell27) with 6 auxiliary full-cell/half-cell reference files (CH_FC_POCV.mat, CH_HC_anode.mat, CH_HC_cathode.mat, DCH_FC_POCV.mat, DCH_HC_anode.mat, DHC_HC_cathode.mat - characterization/reference files, not six additional independently identified batteries) plus one oddly-named TPG3.8-cell14.mat. The closeness of 27 to the registry's 28 is partly coincidental: real cells are undercounted, offset by these non-cell files. The prior protocol summary incorrectly included 1C; the three author READMEs instead state C/4 or C/2 cycling. Recorded C-rate maxima refer to the explicitly stated cycling/reference constant-current rates; pulse-characterization amplitudes are not specified in those lists. Charging profile: the charge rate is fixed within a cell but differs between the cycling groups. The paper (Raj et al. 2020; full text read) is the study of part 1 and confirms the cell: Panasonic NCR18650BD (the cell is called NCA/graphite in the text and carbon in Table 1), 3 Ah rated, 2.5-4.2 V, maximum charge current 1.5 A, maximum continuous discharge 10 A, at a constant 24 C in a Binder thermal chamber (Maccor 4200 tester, BioLogic MPG205 for EIS). It tested 12 cells, 3 in each of 4 groups: groups 1 and 2 cycle one day then store five days, groups 3 and 4 cycle two days then store ten days, cycling at C/2 (groups 1 and 3) or C/4 (groups 2 and 4) between 0 and 100% SoC (2.5-4.2 V) at constant current, calendar ageing at 90% of actual SoC, C-rates always relative to the rated capacity. Reference performance tests every 48 cycles: 3 h rest, CCCV capacity test at C/2 to C/60 (0.05 A), pseudo-OCV at C/24, then pulse-power tests at 80, 50 and 20% SoC with 10 s C/2 (1.5 A) charge and discharge pulses and 3.33C (10 A) discharge pulses; GITT at C/2 and EIS at beginning, middle (384 days) and end of life, plus CR2032 half cells from a fresh cell. So 3.33C (10 A, the rated maximum continuous discharge) is the highest rate and applies to short pulses, which is why discharge_c_rate_max is 3.33 here and not the C/2 cycling rate. The paper's 12 cells are a part of the 20 numbered cells in the three data parts; the readme and landing page counts of 3 do not describe the whole dataset. Temperature is a chamber setpoint; the paper mentions no cell sensor. The protocol class is 'mixed' because cycling and calendar storage are combined. Rate combinations: the ageing cycles apply constant current in both directions, at C/2 for groups 1 and 3 and C/4 for groups 2 and 4 (the paper gives one rate per group for charge and discharge); the reference tests charge CC-CV at C/2.
